title: Jewelled Rice
subtitle: Persian saffron rice with fruit and nuts
excerpt: Fluffy saffron-stained basmati rice scattered with barberries, toasted nuts, and strips of orange peel. Served at celebrations across Iran. It looks beautiful and tastes as good as it looks.
sourceNotes: Jewelled rice, or morasa polo, is a celebratory dish in Persian cuisine. It is served at weddings and Nowruz, the Persian New Year. Each ingredient in the topping is chosen for colour and symbolic meaning.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the rice base ahead. Add the toppings just before serving.

content.text: Parboil the rice first, then steam it with a cloth under the lid. This is the classic Persian method and gives the rice its famously light, separate grains. Do not skip the parboil step.

items.prepNote: rinsed until water runs clear, then soaked 30 minutes
zest only, cut into thin strips and blanched twice
use a mix of barberries, cranberries, or raisins

content.text: Boil a large pot of well-salted water. Add the soaked, drained rice. Parboil for 5 to 6 minutes until the rice is almost cooked but has a firm centre. Drain.
In the same pot, melt half the butter. Spread a thin layer of rice over the base.
Pile the rest of the rice into a mound on top. Make a few holes in the rice with a spoon handle.
Wrap the lid in a clean cloth and place on the pot. Steam on low heat for 30 minutes. The cloth absorbs steam and keeps the rice dry.
While the rice steams, fry the onion in oil until golden and caramelised. Add the orange peel, barberries, and cinnamon. Stir for 2 minutes.
Mix the saffron water with a large spoonful of the cooked rice. Set aside for garnish.
Transfer the rice to a platter. Top with the onion mixture and toasted pine nuts. Scatter saffron rice over the top for colour.

items.fix: The rice must still have a firm centre after parboiling. Steam finishes the cooking. Drain thoroughly before steaming.

items.cause: Not enough fat in the base or heat too low
items.fix: A higher heat for the first 5 minutes sets the crust. Then reduce to low for the steaming. A nonstick pot helps.

items.cause: Saffron not bloomed properly or low quality
items.fix: Use a generous pinch and steep in very hot water for at least 10 minutes. Good saffron turns the water a deep orange.

content.text: Morasa polo, or jewelled rice, is one of Iran's most celebratory dishes. It is served at weddings, Nowruz, and other important occasions. The gems it is named after are the barberries, pistachios, almonds, orange peel, and saffron that make up the topping. Each ingredient is chosen as much for its colour and symbolism as its flavour.
